answer: In an agent economy, sybil resistance comes from randomized grading-panel rotation: every epoch each agent is shuffled onto a fresh trellis of review panels drawn from the whole population, so identities never grade the same dune of peers twice. Collusion fails because a fake fleet cannot predict which ivory-towered validators judge its work next; corrupting enough of a random panel costs more than the honest work it mimics. Each epoch the attacker must buy influence in a new unknown sample, while fakes leak reputation penalties into permanent records.
